model.objective: Minimize query-dependent bytes and decode work while preserving trusted top-k answers and exhaustive proof semantics.
model.claim_boundary: Engineering gates can be passed without proving the mathematical lower bound; the gap entries identify what proof or algorithm is still missing.

startup_entry_gap.lower_bound_definition: The first page can only read routing metadata, aliases, and source registry bytes needed to map a query into a proof-capable route.
startup_entry_gap.gap_to_lower_bound: Metadata is already separated from local indexes and full shards, but the routed entry payload is still a practical JSON contract rather than an entropy-coded minimal decision table.
startup_entry_gap.next_algorithmic_step: Delta-code source/query routing tables and measure whether a compact finite-state router beats the current manifest plus directory bytes without hurting debuggability.
startup_entry_gap.correctness_guard: Runtime contract must keep startup_loads_local_indexes=false and startup_loads_full_shards=false.
startup_entry_gap.stop_condition: Stop when further byte reductions change only encoding overhead and do not reduce the set of information required to choose the route.

route_planning_gap.lower_bound_definition: Routing must inspect only the cheapest source/local-index summaries whose expected utility can still alter the first trusted or top-k result set.
route_planning_gap.gap_to_lower_bound: The planner emits expected byte costs and phase-local selections, but the route policy is still hand-calibrated rather than learned from an optimal decision rule.
route_planning_gap.next_algorithmic_step: Fit an offline decision policy on the evaluation corpus with byte cost as the Lagrange multiplier, then keep only policies that preserve task quality.
route_planning_gap.correctness_guard: Every route still has to produce a complete coverage ledger before exhaustive claims.
route_planning_gap.stop_condition: Stop when alternative route policies cannot reduce phase bytes at equal quality and equal proof completeness.

first_trusted_gap.lower_bound_definition: The first trusted phase needs enough evidence to show at least one justified result and no bytes for later hydration or exhaustive proof.
first_trusted_gap.gap_to_lower_bound: The phase is byte-gated and query-path decode improved versus baseline, but the remaining gap is proving that no loaded local-index byte is irrelevant to the first trusted result.
first_trusted_gap.next_algorithmic_step: Add per-term contribution accounting for first-result eligibility and drop zero-contribution term blocks.
first_trusted_gap.correctness_guard: A first trusted result must carry source, score reason, and enough local evidence to be reproducible.
first_trusted_gap.stop_condition: Stop when contribution accounting proves every loaded term block can affect the displayed first result.

top_results_hydrated_gap.lower_bound_definition: Top-k hydration needs postings and document evidence only for candidates whose upper bound can enter the visible top result set.
top_results_hydrated_gap.gap_to_lower_bound: Top results are separated from proof completion, but candidate upper bounds are not yet serialized as a formal certificate that every skipped block is dominated.
top_results_hydrated_gap.next_algorithmic_step: Persist block-level score upper bounds and emit a top-k dominance certificate for skipped blocks.
top_results_hydrated_gap.correctness_guard: Hydrated top results must remain identical under exhaustive verification for the measured query suite.
top_results_hydrated_gap.stop_condition: Stop when every skipped block has a recorded upper bound below the kth hydrated result score.

proof_complete_certificate_gap.lower_bound_definition: A complete proof should read only no-match certificates and unresolved shard evidence required to justify exhaustive completeness.
proof_complete_certificate_gap.gap_to_lower_bound: Correctness is complete, but proof completion can still approach a full-shard read. The mathematical lower bound is a certificate stream, not full document hydration.
proof_complete_certificate_gap.next_algorithmic_step: Separate false-positive filter pressure from true-match shard pressure, then generate doc/postings or hot-query certificates for true-match-heavy broad queries.
proof_complete_certificate_gap.correctness_guard: No-match, failed-shard, and pending-ledger refusal tests must stay green before replacing full proof reads.
proof_complete_certificate_gap.stop_condition: Stop when proof bytes are proportional to certificate entropy plus matched shard evidence, not total shard corpus size.

full_shard_dependency_gap.lower_bound_definition: Full shard bodies are outside the first-result and top-k lower bound; they are only needed when the user asks for complete proof or full document hydration.
full_shard_dependency_gap.gap_to_lower_bound: The serving path no longer depends on full shards for startup or early results, but exhaustive proof still has a full-shard fallback.
full_shard_dependency_gap.next_algorithmic_step: Split proof certificates from full document bodies and make full bodies lazy even during proof completion.
full_shard_dependency_gap.correctness_guard: Document hydration must still produce byte-identical titles, URLs, snippets, and attachment evidence.
full_shard_dependency_gap.stop_condition: Stop when proof_complete has zero full-body dependency except for matched documents shown to the user.

packed_index_decode_gap.lower_bound_definition: Index decode should touch only terms and impact blocks that can affect routing, first trusted results, or top-k ranking.
packed_index_decode_gap.gap_to_lower_bound: Packed selective decode is active on the hot query path, but block metadata is still decoded at artifact granularity rather than at the exact surviving term/block frontier.
packed_index_decode_gap.next_algorithmic_step: Move to block directory offsets with direct term/block seeks and SIMD/WASM-friendly score scans.
packed_index_decode_gap.correctness_guard: Packed and JSON decoders must produce equivalent term statistics for sampled and task queries.
packed_index_decode_gap.stop_condition: Stop when decode work is asymptotically tied to matched query terms and unpruned impact blocks.

topk_pruning_gap.lower_bound_definition: Top-k retrieval should visit postings only while their block upper bound can beat the current kth competitive threshold.
topk_pruning_gap.gap_to_lower_bound: Dynamic pruning is present, but the report does not yet prove that the pruning order is optimal for every query under the scoring function.
topk_pruning_gap.next_algorithmic_step: Record WAND/BMW-style upper-bound ledgers per query and compare visited postings against an oracle ordering.
topk_pruning_gap.correctness_guard: Pruned postings must have an upper bound below the competitive threshold recorded at prune time.
topk_pruning_gap.stop_condition: Stop when the visited posting count matches the oracle lower envelope within tie-handling noise.

persistent_cache_gap.lower_bound_definition: After immutable artifacts are cached, a repeated query should perform zero network bytes beyond validation and any changed content-hash paths.
persistent_cache_gap.gap_to_lower_bound: Warm network bytes are gated locally; remaining lower-bound work is CPU decode reuse and browser-level confirmation when a browser report is missing.
persistent_cache_gap.next_algorithmic_step: Persist decoded packed-index pages and reuse score-session state across repeated same-version queries.
persistent_cache_gap.correctness_guard: Content-hash changes must invalidate stale cached artifacts and decoded pages.
persistent_cache_gap.stop_condition: Stop when warm repeat queries have zero immutable network bytes and no repeated decode for unchanged pages.

attachment_semantics_gap.lower_bound_definition: Attachment evidence should be summarized by the smallest semantic fields required to justify search results without downloading attachments.
attachment_semantics_gap.gap_to_lower_bound: Attachment evidence is summarized, but there is no per-query proof that the summary is the minimal sufficient statistic for attachment relevance.
attachment_semantics_gap.next_algorithmic_step: Add query-term-to-attachment-evidence attribution and measure dropped attachment fields against task quality.
attachment_semantics_gap.correctness_guard: Attachment-bearing results must still expose source-level evidence and never imply unread attachment contents.
attachment_semantics_gap.stop_condition: Stop when every retained attachment field has a measured ranking or trust contribution.

ranking_calibration_gap.lower_bound_definition: Ranking should preserve only the scoring features whose marginal information changes user-visible order or trust at the target quality level.
ranking_calibration_gap.gap_to_lower_bound: Quality gates exist, but ranking weights are still an engineered policy rather than a Pareto-optimal model over relevance, trust, recency, and byte cost.
ranking_calibration_gap.next_algorithmic_step: Run ablations over ranking features and fit byte-aware weights that stay on the quality Pareto frontier.
ranking_calibration_gap.correctness_guard: Task-query expectations, smoke queries, and negative proof behavior must remain satisfied.
ranking_calibration_gap.stop_condition: Stop when removing or reweighting any retained feature lowers measured relevance or trust at equal byte cost.

browser_resource_gap.lower_bound_definition: The browser should request only phase-required immutable artifacts, render without layout/console regressions, and reuse cached artifacts across repeated queries.
browser_resource_gap.gap_to_lower_bound: Browser verification is recorded only when the external browser report is present; the CLI report must not claim final browser lower-bound evidence without it.
browser_resource_gap.next_algorithmic_step: Keep browser automation as a mandatory artifact and compare network/resource traces per phase.
browser_resource_gap.correctness_guard: Browser evidence must include desktop/mobile viewports, console status, result rendering, and warm-cache behavior.
browser_resource_gap.stop_condition: Stop when browser resource traces match the phase model and stay stable across target viewports.

evidence.planner: Planner telemetry includes route expected_cost_bytes, selected expected_uncached bytes, cache state per local index, and phase-specific local index selections.

4.evidence: Measured queries report proof ledger complete with zero pending/failed shards; runtime tests cover no-match proof, failed shard refusal, and cancelled pending-ledger refusal.

evidence.note: Runtime local-index parse/decode uses query-term selective packed decoders; family-level tables retain full-decode diagnostics, while query-path tables gate the actual phase-selected hot path.
Packed binary light terms plus metadata JSON are used for query planning; packed binary light/body indexes are scored by the stateful Rust/WASM top-k retrieval session in the browser worker.

decision.reason: The browser runtime can consume Rust/WASM stateful score entries directly. On the full packed body workload, the Rust/WASM session score bridge was 0.175x the TypeScript selective retrieval kernel for the same artifact format, query set, and global top-k pruning state.

evidence.cache_invalidation_test: Changed content-hash artifact paths are treated as cold cache misses.

10.evidence: Smoke queries, task queries, measured cold queries, warm cache queries, and a negative query are represented when full report mode is used.
